answer: A practical sybil defense is to tie each agent identity to a non-transferable stake plus a verifiable work record. Before an agent can vote or earn, it must complete a long voyage of small, peer-attested tasks, each check recorded on-chain. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then costs real stake and real compute for every one, while a single fake vote creates only a tiny ripple in the total. Like a canyon carved slowly by water, reputation must be earned over time and cannot be bought in bulk or copied across identities, so an attacker cost grows linearly with every fake added.
